memos.headline: AAPL and MSFT Lead at 52-Week Highs While UNH and CAT Show Deteriorating Relative Strength
memos.body: I see a clear two-tier market today. AAPL is sitting at its 52-week high with zero drawdown, +8.4% relative strength vs SPY over 4 weeks, and RSI 65.7 — strong but not yet overbought — making it the cleanest trend in the universe. MSFT is similarly powerful, +8.5% above its 50-day and +19.5% above its 200-day, with 12-week relative strength of +30.9% vs SPY, though the extended stretch from moving averages warrants tighter risk management. On the other side, UNH is in a clear downtrend with RSI 39.9, -5.7% below its 50-day, -11.7% over 12 weeks, and -15.1% relative strength vs SPY over that period — I want no part of that until it reclaims its 50-day average. CAT is the worst relative performer in the group at -20.6% vs SPY over 12 weeks and -22.8% from its 52-week high, suggesting a broken intermediate trend despite the recent 1-week bounce. NVDA and XOM sit in the middle with constructive but less decisive setups.

views.note: At 52-week high with strong relative strength and RSI 65.7; trend intact above 50d mean (~$322); would reassess on a close below $322.

Massive 12-week relative strength of +30.9% vs SPY and RSI 63.2, but +8.5% above 50d mean is stretched; a pullback to the 50d (~$476) would be a better entry, and a close below $476 would change my view.
Constructive longer-term trend (+12.8% above 200d) but 4-week relative strength is negative and RSI 55.2 is middling; need a breakout above the 52-week high (~$236) to get more constructive.
RSI 39.9, -5.7% below 50d mean, -15.1% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks — clear intermediate downtrend; would reconsider only on a sustained close above the 50d (~$399).
Worst relative performer at -20.6% vs SPY over 12 weeks with -22.8% drawdown from 52-week high; broken trend until it reclaims the $830-$840 area near its 50d mean.

12-week relative strength of +14.4% vs SPY is notable and price is above both moving averages, but RSI 48.7 and flat 26-week return (+0.6%) temper conviction; a close below the 200d (~$148) would negate.
Below 50d mean, RSI 44.5, and -12.1% drawdown suggest a name losing momentum; flat relative strength over 12 weeks means no edge either way — need a reclaim of the 50d (~$256) to turn constructive.
Sitting right on its 50d mean with RSI 49.7 and -14.6% drawdown from highs; 12-week relative strength of -8.2% vs SPY is weak, making this a show-me name until it breaks above $360.
RSI 41.7 and -3.2% 4-week relative strength suggest near-term weakness, but still +6.8% above 200d; watching the 200d (~$321) as the line in the sand.
Flat on every timeframe with price hugging both moving averages and RSI 50.6 — the definition of trendless; low ATR of 1.48% limits opportunity.

memos.headline: Hyper-scalers and NVDA deliver extraordinary earnings growth; XOM and PG show cash-flow compression
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe. NVDA posted $96.2B in quarterly revenue (+105.9% YoY) with a 62.0% net margin, while GOOGL printed a remarkable 93.7% net margin on $119.8B of revenue—both numbers I want to own. AMZN's net income surged 244.9% YoY to $62.65B on a 31.2% margin, and MSFT closed its fiscal year with $35.77B in net income (+31.3% YoY) at a 39.7% margin, confirming durable earnings power across the mega-cap tech complex. On the other side, XOM's net income fell 45.8% YoY to $4.18B on a thin 4.9% margin, and PG's net income declined 15.8% YoY with revenue growing only 1.5%—classic cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for. I would revisit XOM if Q2 margins recover above 8% and PG if organic revenue growth reaccelerates above 4%.

views.note: Revenue doubling YoY with 62% net margins is unmatched earnings power; I'd reassess only if margins contract below 50%.
93.7% net margin on $119.8B revenue with minimal debt ($14.8B) signals extraordinary profitability, though the margin level likely includes one-time items I want to verify.
Full-year Q4 revenue of $90B (+17.7% YoY) with 39.7% net margin and moderate $40.3B debt demonstrates durable, high-quality earnings.
Net income up 244.9% YoY to $62.65B with margin expanding to 31.2% shows operating leverage kicking in, though $133B in total debt warrants monitoring.
Revenue +16.4% YoY to $109.4B with 27.2% net margin is solid, but $82.3B in debt and slower growth relative to peers temper my conviction.
Revenue +24% YoY and net income +64.9% with a 17.5% margin show strong cyclical momentum, but I'd turn cautious if backlog data weakens.
Net income +41.2% YoY and 36.9% margin are impressive for a bank, but $460.5B in total debt and credit-cycle sensitivity keep me neutral.
Revenue essentially flat (+0.4% YoY) with a thin 4.9% margin despite 61% net income recovery suggests cost-driven improvement that may not sustain.
Net income down 45.8% YoY to $4.18B on a 4.9% margin is textbook cash-flow compression; I'd reconsider above an 8% margin.
Revenue +1.5% with net income declining 15.8% and margin compressing to 14.4% signals deteriorating earnings quality in a premium-valued staple.

memos.headline: Fed Pausing at 4% While 10y Yields Surge to 5.17%: Stagflationary Tilt Favors Defensives and Energy Over Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see a macro regime that is increasingly uncomfortable for long-duration assets. The Fed has raised the upper bound 25bp over the past three months to 4.00%, yet CPI is running at 3.4% YoY with essentially zero progress over the last quarter — suggesting the Fed is in a reluctant pause-to-hike posture rather than anywhere near easing. The 10y yield at 5.17% is up nearly 100bp over the past year, a punishing move for equity duration, while the 10y-2y spread at +31bp has flattened 28bp YoY, signaling the market is pricing persistent policy tightness. The labor market remains solid at 4.1% unemployment (down 20bp over 3m and 12m), which removes any urgency for the Fed to cut and keeps the stagflationary risk alive. A CPI print that breaks convincingly below 3% or an unemployment spike above 4.5% would change my regime call toward easing, but until then I am positioned defensively.

views.note: High-multiple consumer tech is directly pressured by 5%+ long-end yields and a Fed that shows no inclination to ease.
Duration-sensitive growth faces headwinds from the 100bp YoY rise in the 10y yield and sticky 3.4% inflation keeping the Fed on hold.
Highest-duration name in the universe is most vulnerable to the 5.17% 10y yield and no near-term rate relief.
Banks benefit from a steep-enough curve (+31bp 10y-2y) and solid employment, but the flattening trend and elevated long rates cap upside.
Energy tends to outperform in stagflationary regimes with sticky inflation and solid labor demand; real rates are less of a headwind for cash-flow-rich commodity producers.
Staples offer defensive positioning with pricing power in a 3.4% CPI environment and lower duration sensitivity than tech.
Healthcare defensive with relatively low duration; benefits from steady employment keeping insurance enrollment robust at 4.1% unemployment.
Cyclical exposure is supported by low unemployment but threatened by rising real rates and a potential growth slowdown if the Fed is forced to hike further.
Growth-oriented valuation is pressured by the 5.17% 10y yield; consumer spending resilience is the offset but not enough in this rate regime.
Ad-driven revenue is more cyclically resilient than pure growth peers, but elevated yields still weigh on multiples; I lack conviction either way.

memos.headline: NVDA Post-Earnings Momentum and CAT Earnings Beat Stand Out; Limited Sentiment Signal Elsewhere
memos.body: I see two clear narrative-driven moves in the universe this cycle. NVDA reported results on 8/26 and the stock jumped +8.7% the next day, followed by a material agreement filing and an additional 'Other Events' 8-K on 9/3—this cluster of filings suggests sustained positive attention, though three weeks later the initial euphoria is likely priced. CAT's 8/4 earnings release drove a +5.6% one-day move, and the subsequent 9/1 material agreement filing keeps the narrative constructive, but again the price reaction is nearly two months old. AMZN has two filings in September including a leadership change and an 'Other Events' disclosure, which could signal a narrative shift worth monitoring but lacks a clear directional tone signal yet. AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, and UNH each had single routine-looking filings (officer changes, Reg FD, other events) that do not suggest any meaningful sentiment inflection from my vantage point.

views.note: Clustered positive filings and +8.7% earnings reaction suggest strong sentiment, though much is likely priced after three weeks.
Earnings beat drove +5.6% and follow-on material agreement keeps narrative positive, but the move is nearly two months stale.
Leadership change and Other Events filing in September could mark a narrative shift, but no clear directional tone signal yet.
Single 8-K/A on officer departure/appointment is routine and provides no actionable sentiment signal.
Reg FD disclosure on 9/2 is standard and does not indicate a sentiment inflection.
Single Other Events filing in August is too generic to derive a sentiment view.
Reg FD disclosure on 9/8 is routine with no evidence of tone shift.

memos.headline: Surging Oil Prices Signal Energy-Security Stress; Export-Control Overhang Persists for Semis
memos.body: I see two dominant geopolitical signals as of today. First, WTI crude at $95.88/bbl is up 34% over three months and 11% in the last month alone, pointing to a supply-side squeeze likely tied to OPEC+ discipline or sanctions-related disruptions—this is a structural tailwind for XOM and a margin headwind for energy-intensive logistics names like AMZN and CAT. Second, while the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has fallen sharply (279 vs ~465 three months ago) and VIX sits at a benign 15.67, the absolute level of policy uncertainty remains elevated, and NVDA filed two 8-Ks in quick succession (Aug 17 and Sep 3), which I read as potential disclosure around export-control developments or customer-notification obligations. I have moderate conviction that the oil move is more structural than seasonal, but I lack granular detail on the specific policy catalysts behind the NVDA and MSFT filings, so my confidence on semis is lower. A reversal in my oil view would require a credible OPEC+ production increase or a sanctions-relief deal; on semis, any broadening of China chip-export restrictions would turn me more negative on NVDA.

views.note: WTI up 34% in 3 months to ~$96 is a structural energy-security premium that directly lifts XOM earnings and free cash flow.
Two 8-K filings in three weeks suggest possible export-control or regulatory disclosure; until content is clear, I stay neutral despite falling policy uncertainty.
Rising energy costs pressure logistics margins, but falling policy uncertainty and tight credit spreads limit broader macro risk for now.
Energy capex cycle benefits CAT equipment demand; elevated oil prices historically drive upstream investment, though higher input costs partially offset.
Reg FD filing in early September may relate to AI-infrastructure or cloud-policy disclosures; without specifics, geopolitical risk is ambiguous.
Domestic healthcare policy uncertainty is declining per the EPU index, but the Sep 8 Reg FD filing could signal regulatory engagement; no clear directional call.

Heavy cash (~40%) reflects the tension between powerful earnings growth and a hostile rate regime with 10y yields at 5.17%.
